The golden rule

scenes.vo: Step by step: First, Networks (chains): the same token (for example U.S.D.C.) can exist on several blockchains: Ethereum (the main one, higher fees) and cheaper Layer 2 networks such as Arbitrum, Base and Optimism. Next, the golden rule: the network you withdraw on must match a network your wallet (or the receiving service) supports. Sending on the wrong network can mean lost funds. Then, Gas: every transaction pays a small network fee in the network's gas token. On Ethereum and its Layer 2s that's ETH. Without a little ETH on the network you're using, you can't move anything. Also, your wallet address is usually the same on Ethereum and its Layer 2s, but your balances are separate per network. Switch networks in your wallet to see them. On top of that, in your wallet, copy your address (use the copy button; never type it).

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: Later, a swap on Arbitrum costs a few cents in gas.
The same swap on Ethereum might cost a few dollars, more when the network is…

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Withdrawing $100 of ETH to Arbitrum: exchange withdrawal fee about $0.10 to $1. Later, a swap on Arbitrum costs a few cents in gas. The same swap on Ethereum might cost a few dollars, more when the network is busy. That's why beginners learn on Layer 2s.

scenes.q: What's the golden rule of withdrawals?
scenes.a: The network you send on must be one the receiving wallet or service supports.
